name: Långsjö Parish
region: Dalarna, on a lake north of Siljan
description: Långsjö is a lakeside parish of closely built villages of grey and red timber, where the farms have been divided by inheritance so many times that each family's strips of field are barely wide enough to turn a plough. In summer the women and girls take the cattle to the fäbod, the summer pastures in the forest hills, and live there until autumn. The men go away to work on the railways and in the towns, and come back for midsummer.
seasonNotes: June, around midsummer. The nights do not grow dark at all, only a long amber dusk that turns straight into dawn. The midsummer pole is raised in the village meadow, dressed in birch and flowers, and people dance on the grass all night. The cattle went up to the summer pastures at the start of the month. Haymaking has not yet begun; the meadows are full of flowers and mosquitoes swarm by the water.
travel: From Uppsala by coach to Gävle, then by the Gävle-Dala railway to Falun and on by coach and lake steamer, about three days.
publicFacts: The great land redistribution (storskifte) of the parish is under way, and surveyors are redrawing the strips of every farm; it has caused bitter quarrels.
Many young men of Långsjö go away every year to work as navvies on the railways or as masons in Stockholm.
Families row to church across the lake in long church boats, racing each other on midsummer day.
The fäbod at Björnberget is used by six farms of the east village; the women stay there from early June until September.
The parish is known for its painted furniture and clocks, sold at the markets in the south.
Two Långsjö girls emigrated to Minnesota last year and their letters are read aloud in the village.
The new vicar is a strict man of the revival who has banned dancing at the parsonage and frowns at the midsummer pole.

places.name: Långsjö Church
places.description: The white stone church stands on a headland reaching into the lake, with the church boat landing and its row of boathouses below. The lake glitters blue in the endless light and the churchyard grass is high with buttercups. Inside, the walls are painted with bright Dalarna flowers and biblical figures in local dress. Swallows dart in and out of the bell tower.

affordances.name: Sacristy
affordances.description: A small vaulted room off the chancel where the vicar robes.

contains.name: Vestment cupboard
contains.description: A tall cupboard of chasubles, the surplice and spare altar candles.

contains.name: Parish chest
contains.description: An ancient iron-banded chest with three locks for the communion silver and old deeds.

affordances.name: Bell tower
affordances.description: Steep ladders up to the bells, bird droppings on the beams, wind through the louvres.

affordances.name: Church loft
affordances.description: The dusty space above the vaults, full of broken pews and old hatchments.

places.name: Långsjö Parsonage
places.ownerRole: the vicar of the parish, who lives here and serves the church
places.description: The parsonage is a long yellow manor-like house among lilacs and apple trees, its windows thrown open to the summer air. Bees hum in the garden and a maid is beating rugs on the line. The vicar's study looks out over the lake. Even in June the room where the parish registers are kept smells cold and of old paper.

affordances.name: Vicar's study
affordances.description: The study where the vicar writes sermons and receives parishioners.

contains.name: Vicar's desk
contains.description: A desk under the window with sermon drafts.

contains.name: Locked drawer
contains.description: A locked drawer for private letters and certificates waiting to be signed.

contains.name: Bookshelves
contains.description: Shelves of postils, Luther, hymnals and back numbers of church journals.

affordances.name: Parish registers
affordances.description: The church books: household examination rolls, birth, death and moving registers.

affordances.name: Parlour
affordances.description: The parsonage parlour where the vicar's wife receives.

affordances.name: Kitchen
affordances.description: The parsonage kitchen.

affordances.name: Maids' room
affordances.description: The room of the parsonage maids.

affordances.name: Glebe barn
affordances.description: The barn of the glebe farm.

affordances.name: Glebe cowshed
affordances.description: The parsonage cowshed.

affordances.name: Parsonage garden
affordances.description: An orchard and kitchen garden, the vicar's pride.

places.name: Olsgården in Västbyn
places.ownerRole: the Ols family, freeholders of the farm in Västbyn
places.description: A farm in the crowded west village, its grey log buildings pressed so close to the neighbours' that you can step from one yard to the next. Flowers have been tucked above the doors for midsummer. The yard is quiet; the cattle are away at the summer pasture and the men are off at work. The old grandmother sits on the step carding wool in the sun.

affordances.name: Farmyard
affordances.description: The yard between the buildings, trodden mud and a woodpile.

affordances.name: Main room
affordances.description: The everyday room: open hearth, long table, wall beds and the loom in the corner.

contains.name: Open hearth
contains.description: The whitewashed corner hearth with its iron pot-hook.

affordances.name: Best room
affordances.description: The cold best room, painted furniture, the family Bible and a clock from Mora.

contains.name: Dowry chest
contains.description: A painted chest with the wife's linen and the year of her wedding on the lid.

affordances.name: Farmhands' chamber
affordances.description: A bare chamber with two beds and the hands' own chests.

affordances.name: Cowshed
affordances.description: A low dark byre, warm with cattle breath.

affordances.name: Stable
affordances.description: A stable for the farm horse or horses.

affordances.name: Barn
affordances.description: A timber barn for the harvest.

contains.name: Hayloft
contains.description: The hay store over the barn floor, reached by a ladder.

affordances.name: Threshing barn
affordances.description: A threshing barn (loge) where the grain is threshed with flails through the autumn.

affordances.name: Root cellar
affordances.description: A root cellar dug into the slope, holding potatoes, turnips and the milk.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A well with a sweep pole and a wooden bucket.

affordances.name: Bathhouse
affordances.description: A small log bastu with a stone oven, also used for drying malt and flax.

places.name: The Fäbod at Björnberget
places.ownerRole: the dairymaid who keeps the shieling for the village farms through the summer
places.description: High on a forest hill three hours' walk from the village, a cluster of small grey huts stands in a clearing of rich grass, ringed by spruce. Cowbells clank in the trees and goats climb on the roofs. The women's herding calls echo off the slopes, and smoke rises from the hut where milk is boiled down into whey cheese. A clear stream runs past the huts, cold as winter.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: The fäbod hut: a hearth for boiling milk, a bench, a narrow bed and wooden pails stacked to dry.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: The hearth, smoke-blackened, a pot simmering.

contains.name: Clothes chest
contains.description: The family's one chest for Sunday clothes and papers.

contains.name: Loose board
contains.description: A loose floorboard by the bed where a few coins can be kept.

affordances.name: Byre
affordances.description: A long low shed where the herd is shut in at night against the forest.

affordances.name: Earth cellar
affordances.description: A turf-roofed earth cellar for potatoes.

affordances.name: Well
affordances.description: A shallow well or a spring-fed pit with a bucket.

affordances.name: Potato patch
affordances.description: A small fenced patch by the huts where the grass is grown for winter hay.

places.name: The Stream Mills
places.ownerRole: the miller who grinds for the village farms at the stream mills
places.description: Along a steep stream that tumbles down to the lake, a row of tiny mill huts perch on stilts over the water, one for each group of farms. Each has a small horizontal wheel that rattles when the water is let onto it, the old skvaltkvarn sound. In summer the stream is low and only one mill is grinding. Ferns and moss grow thick on the wet stones.

affordances.name: Waterwheel and race
affordances.description: A small horizontal wheel under the hut, its paddles worn smooth, rattling in a spout of water.

affordances.name: Mill pond
affordances.description: A small pool behind a weir of stones and turf, clear enough to see the trout.

affordances.name: Millstones
affordances.description: The stones, hopper and gearing, everything white with meal.

affordances.name: Grain loft
affordances.description: The loft where sacks wait to be ground.

affordances.name: Mill store
affordances.description: A store of spare cogs, pick-hammers for dressing the stones and sacks.

affordances.name: Miller's house
affordances.description: The miller's cottage beside the mill, with its own hearth.

places.name: The Village Smithy
places.description: The smithy is at the edge of the meadow, its door wide open, and the smith is making nails and hinges for the new barns the land redistribution demands. Boys gather to watch the sparks. The forge smoke drifts across the meadow where the midsummer pole stands. Inside, the light is a dark orange compared with the white glare outside.

affordances.name: Forge
affordances.description: The hearth and bellows, the anvil on its stump, the quench trough.

affordances.name: Workshop
affordances.description: The bench and racks of tongs, hammers and half-finished work.

affordances.name: Coal shed
affordances.description: A shed of charcoal and bar iron from the works.

affordances.name: Smith's cottage
affordances.description: The smith's one-room cottage across the yard.

contains.name: Smith's chest
contains.description: The smith's own chest of papers and good clothes.

places.name: Kerstin's Cottage
places.ownerRole: Kerstin, the wise woman the cottage is named for
places.description: A small red cottage stands alone by a marshy inlet of the lake, with a garden of tall flowering plants fenced against the goats. Midsummer is the night to gather herbs, and bunches of fresh plants are laid out to dry on cloths everywhere. Dragonflies hover over the reeds. The woman who lives here is known to everyone and visited by many after dark.

affordances.name: Cottage room
affordances.description: A single low room, dim and smelling of smoke and herbs.

contains.name: Hearth
contains.description: A hearth with a brew always going.

affordances.name: Herb store
affordances.description: Bunches of drying herbs from the rafters, jars of salve and dried roots.

contains.name: Remedy cupboard
contains.description: A small cupboard of bottles, wrapped in rag and labelled in a crabbed hand.

contains.name: Small box
contains.description: A small wooden box kept on a high shelf.

affordances.name: Herb garden
affordances.description: A fenced garden of medicinal plants.

affordances.name: Earth cellar
affordances.description: A small earth cellar.

affordances.name: Spring
affordances.description: A spring-fed well with a cup on a string.

affordances.name: Hollow in the wall
affordances.description: A hollow behind a loose log in the wall.
